title: Joining Charlie Barnet and the freedom to play
summary: Barnet gives him complete freedom, which Leeman, who knew the Ellington book by heart, uses to develop his own style.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: got a call, and I went in and was interviewed by Charlie Barnet, which twisted my life completely at that moment.
Because for the next year and a half, I didn't do anything but one nighters.
What were you saying about Charlie Barnet?

My association with Charlie Barnet was 1940. The last of '39 and '40 -- and he gave me all the freedom in the world, all the freedom. The band had been burned out in California; Duke Ellington had given them all the rope that they needed -- that was the style of band that they wanted, and all my life I knew this, I could have played with Duke Ellington without any parts because I knew every part by heart, and I wanted Charlie Barnet who just said play -- and he gave me all the freedom to develop my own style at that point in life.
I could try out my little things that I learned a lot of them from other drummers. You compile, you know?
